after: ## Where this fits in the syllabus
alt: A scenario from any later topic sits at the centre, examined through three lenses: perspectives (which environmental value system lies behind a position), systems (inputs, outputs and feedback loops) and sustainability (whether use stays within natural income).
caption: Apply perspectives, systems and sustainability together to any later topic.

alt: Cultural, religious, economic and socio-political context shape an environmental value system. Three categories follow: ecocentrism values nature for its own sake, anthropocentrism manages the environment for human benefit, and technocentrism trusts technology and ingenuity to solve problems.
caption: Name the EVS only with evidence from the scenario.

alt: Two feedback loops in which a system’s output affects its own input. Negative feedback is stabilising: a graph shows a disturbance followed by a return to equilibrium. Positive feedback is amplifying: a graph shows the system moving further and further from its original state.
caption: Negative and positive describe the direction of the effect, not whether it is good or bad.

alt: Three systems with dashed boundaries. An open system exchanges both energy and matter across its boundary; a closed system exchanges only energy; an isolated system exchanges neither.
caption: What crosses the boundary defines the type of system.

alt: Graph of rate of use over time against a flat line for natural income. While consumption stays below natural income, use is sustainable; when consumption rises above it, the threshold is crossed and natural capital is depleted. Boxes define natural capital as the stock and natural income as the sustainable yield.
caption: The same resource can move from sustainable to unsustainable use as consumption grows.

after: ## Worked example: applying Topic 1 concepts to a Topic 4 scenario
alt: An aquifer system with rainfall recharge as input (natural income) and extraction for irrigation as a larger output; the stored water is natural capital. A possible positive feedback loop: the water table falls, farmers drill deeper and extract even faster. Side panels judge the use unsustainable and link irrigation-first policy to anthropocentrism and capping extraction to a more ecocentric stance.
caption: One scenario, three lenses: systems, sustainability and perspectives.
